fieldValues.title: A citation-drift guard belongs in scripts/lib/, shared by every citing check, not restated per surface
fieldValues.summary: check-decision-compass-drift.mjs's FORWARD rule (a citation resolves to a real record) and check-rfc-integration.mjs's I-<n> manifest-token resolver were solving the identical sub-problem (does this id/number still name something real?) in two places with two separate normalization copies. When adding a third instance of the same shape (srs-usage.md's I-<n> citations, #490/#670), the number-loading logic was factored into scripts/lib/invariant-numbers.mjs first, and both the new check and check-rfc-integration.mjs's existing resolver were pointed at it, rather than writing a third copy.
fieldValues.rationale: This repo has already paid for the alternative twice: DECISION_MODES was hardcoded in check-rfc-integration.mjs fifty lines below its own correct import of the cell-slug vocabulary (found by an earlier #490 unit, fixed via scripts/lib/decision-modes.mjs); roadmap-model.mjs carried an independent capitalised copy of the twelve Pattern Grid cells (srs#602). Both were the same drift class: a normalization/vocabulary rule with two homes. The Conformance cell's standing preference (rfc-decision-cce3c00e, 'one way over many') makes this a rule, not a style choice — before writing a new check that resolves ids/numbers/slugs against a corpus, check scripts/lib/ for an existing loader over the same corpus first, and if none exists but a sibling check already has the logic inline, extract it rather than copying it. Reopens only if a future consumer of invariant numbers needs a materially different normalization rule (not just a different corpus subset).
